assessments.reasoning: Dewar's title page identifies the author and carries the 1979 copyright. Section 1.1 explicitly presents its introductory listing as a complete SETL program.

challenge.method: Compared the title with the introduction, the SETL-S subset notice on the example page and the date in Shields's later implementation manual.
challenge.results: The introduction names SETL as a programming language and §1.1 presents a complete program written in its teaching subset. Shields cites a SETL reference dated March 12, 1980. That citation leaves the exact relationship between dated document manifestations unresolved.

limitations: 1979 is scoped to the frozen document's copyright, and active is the registry identity state. Claims about invention dates, publication history and the completeness of any particular implementation require separate evidence.
